newsitem.title: UK: NORTH SEA CRUDE STEADY IN PRE-PROGRAMME LULL.
newsitem.headline: NORTH SEA CRUDE STEADY IN PRE-PROGRAMME LULL.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were steady to marginally weaker on Wednesday in a lull before the release of the September loading programmes, traders said.
"There was not much left on offer today," said a physical crude trader. "There should be a few more dates to play with tomorrow."
Most of the major crude loading systems were expected to release schedules for next month on Thursday or Friday.
Volumes were expected to be steady with little maintenance impact on British export streams.

However, Norwegian crudes like Statfjord and Gullfaks will be in shorter supply, with Statfjord B due to close between Aug 25 and Sept 23, and Gullfaks A and B platforms due down between Aug 28 and Sept 15.

Norway's Ekofisk pipeline system has already said it expects to load 21 million barrels comprising 39 cargoes next month. The shorter month accounted for the fall from the 21.79 million barrels expected to load in August, traders said.
Dated Brent markets were lacklustre, with an August 20-22 cargo on offer at -20 to -23 cents and buyers reluctant to shift much from bids of 30 cents below September.
Some demand for physical barrels remained. Two Brent dates were kept by British Petroleum and a third by Wall Street trader J. Aron ahead of the five o'clock deadline.

An August 27-29 Oseberg was sold into Britain for 79 cents above dated Brent on a delivered basis, while a prompt Forties (Aug 19-21) passed between two U.S. majors ex-ship at Dated Brent plus 20 cents equivalent.
The only other physical business seen was a cross-month Ekofisk bought by a French refiner at Dated plus 20 cents.
Brent cash markets were thinly traded with spreads largely static and short-term swaps ending the day slightly weaker.
